rfc_document.details: 685-line comprehensive RFC specification covering format, validation, examples, and adoption strategy

parser_library.details: 364-line Rust library with frontmatter parsing, section detection, and link extraction

validator_cli.details: 702-line CLI tool for validating llms.txt and INDEX.json files

generator.details: 407-line generator with smart section detection and YAML frontmatter support

rendered_rfc_html.notes: RFC exists as markdown, needs HTML rendering for website

community_site.notes: llms.txt.org domain mentioned in RFC but not implemented

example_files.notes: No llms.txt examples from popular projects (Rust, Python, Kubernetes, etc.)

announcement_blog.notes: Blog post needed to announce the standard to community

integration_plugins.notes: IDE plugins and doc generator integrations mentioned in RFC but not implemented

key_observations: RFC specification is comprehensive and well-structured
Core tooling (parser, validator, generator) is largely complete
All code follows strict functional Rust patterns (zero panics)
Test coverage is high for validator and parser
The bead focuses on ecosystem and community adoption, not core implementation
recommended_focus_areas: Create example llms.txt files from 3+ popular projects
Render RFC to HTML and set up basic community site
Write announcement blog post with call to action
Document examples and best practices guide
Consider submitting RFC to standards bodies or community forums

complexity_rationale.reasoning: Multiple deliverables (RFC, validator, parser, generator) already exist (80-95% complete). Remaining work focuses on community-facing deliverables: HTML rendering, community site setup, example generation, and announcement content. This requires content creation, website deployment, and community engagement - diverse tasks justifying full 16-phase TDD workflow.
